answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Baseline. Each identity gets a baseline from its activity nadir across epochs: median task mix, timing, and graph neighbours, verified against a quartz timestamp log for tamper evidence. A new identity whose behaviour deviates beyond a ripple threshold must survive three consecutive epochs of matched consistency before gaining full weight. Sybils must therefore fund and operate each fake identity through multiple epochs, multiplying per-identity cost and exposure time linearly while detection odds compound.
